summary: Two Spring Boot services on Java 21 run on separate EKS nodes with Postgres, the Splunk OTel Collector and OBI off, and a third node runs the load. One Helm value, obi.enabled=true, turns on OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation, and the lab reports the services on the Splunk APM topology that have their own spans, the headline figure, plus all nodes including inferred ones, and the restarts per pod. p95 comes from five rounds with OBI off and five with it on, at about 20 requests a second, with the spread of the OFF rounds as its noise. A logging pipeline then goes onto the Collector, because OBI assigns its own trace IDs and only its exported spans can identify them. Each trace case runs one load round, then reads 30 evenly spaced orders traces exactly 200 seconds after it, retrying misses once and logging each miss's HTTP status. propagate.sh adds the second value, outgoing header propagation, under its own 170-second limit, and both cases report joined traces out of those found in Splunk. The lab also reports the Java agent library OBI maps into each JVM, before and after, and restarts after the second value.
expected: reproduce.sh prints each node's kernel, zero OBI pods, the OBI image on every node, zero OpenTelemetry settings, two warm-up load rounds, five rounds with OBI off, and each pod's UID, restart count and start time, then HERO_RESULT: reproduced.

# One Helm value puts running Java services on EKS onto the Splunk APM map

## What it shows

Two Spring Boot services on Java 21 run on EKS: `orders` calls `inventory` on another node, and `inventory` reads Postgres. A third node runs only the load. In the before state, neither service has any OpenTelemetry instrumentation or setting.

* `reproduce.sh` (BEFORE): installs the Splunk OTel Collector with OBI at its default, off, starts the services, warms them, runs five load rounds with OBI off, and records each pod's UID, restart count and start time.
* `fix.sh` (BUILD): sets `obi.enabled=true` on the Helm release, discards one round while OBI settles, runs five more on the same pods, then adds the Collector tap, runs one more round and reads the service map and 30 traces through the Splunk APM API.
* `propagate.sh`, started by `fix.sh` with its own time limit: sets a second value, outgoing trace propagation, on the same pods and runs one round. Its `read` mode reads each case the same way: 200 seconds after that case's round, 30 traces, then each miss once more.

The headline counts are `services_with_own_spans`, the nodes on the Splunk APM topology that have their own spans, and pod restarts added. `services_on_map` also counts nodes Splunk inferred from a caller. Restarts are reported for each of the three pods. Both come from the first value alone. A replaced pod counts as a restart, because a new pod starts at zero. Restarts after the second value are reported per pod as their own measure.

## What to know first

* OBI, the OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation, is a beta feature in Splunk Observability Cloud. This lab uses chart 0.163.1, which ships OBI 0.15.2. Chart 0.164.0 ships the same OBI.
* The OBI DaemonSet runs privileged with host PID and host network, as root. Check this against your cluster's policy before you plan a rollout. The chart documents a reduced set of capabilities.
* You change nothing in the pod spec. OBI does load its own small Java agent into each running JVM, by default, for TLS tracing, virtual-thread correlation and runtime metrics. The lab reports this for each service, and `javaagent.enabled` controls it.
* OBI instruments every namespace by default, so the map also shows other workloads. The lab counts `orders` and `inventory` by name and prints the rest, including the load client, which OBI traces too.
* The services run on different nodes on purpose. OBI can match a client and server on one node without touching the network, so a same-node result wouldn't tell you what a real cluster does.
* One value puts the services on the map. Outgoing propagation is off by default in OBI, so joining one trace across nodes is a separate value, `obi.env.OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION=headers`. The lab measures each on its own.
* OBI assigns its own trace IDs in these runs, so IDs set by a caller can't identify traces. `k8s/collector-tap.yaml` adds a second Collector pipeline that logs the spans OBI exported, and both trace cases take 30 evenly spaced `orders` trace IDs from it. It goes in after the timed rounds, so no latency figure includes it, and OBI's settings and the export to Splunk don't change. Leave the tap out of your own cluster.
* Each trace case reports joined traces out of the traces found in Splunk, prints what OBI exported, and prints one sample trace's spans. The most services on one trace is a second line: 2 means joined and 1 means separate. Both are real results, and -1 means the case was not measured.

## Run it

`reproduce.sh` also pulls the OBI image onto each node first, so a slow pull can't use up the time of a measured stage.

Set `AWS_REGION`, `LAB_NAME`, `TF_VAR_lab_name` (the same value as `LAB_NAME`), `SPLUNK_REALM`, `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN` (ingest) and `SPLUNK_API_TOKEN` (read). Then run:

```bash
terraform init && terraform apply -auto-approve
./reproduce.sh
./fix.sh
./cleanup.sh
terraform destroy -auto-approve
```

The run uses three `t3.large` nodes in unlimited credit mode, Amazon Linux 2023 on Kubernetes 1.34, and an EKS control plane for about an hour. Splunk's chart documentation names Ubuntu as its tested node OS, and this lab adds a measured result on Amazon Linux 2023. The p95 figure covers OBI at its defaults, including the Java agent it loads, and comes from one cluster and one load rate. Each OFF and ON round prints its p95 next to CPU on the orders, inventory and load nodes, and each side prints its min, median and max. `p95_added_ms` is the median of five ON rounds minus the median of five OFF rounds, at about 20 requests a second, and `p95_noise_ms` is the spread of the OFF rounds. A figure inside that spread is noise, not a cost. Measure your own service before you plan capacity.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, run on a GitHub runner with Docker before AWS is paid for. It renders the real chart, then runs the real OBI
# and Collector images against the lab's own running services. Kubernetes and Splunk don't run here, and the rehearsal covers those.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
source ./lib.sh
mkdir -p c/src c/out c/init c/load

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
open("c/src/pom.xml", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "pom.xml"))
open("c/src/App.java", "w").write(block("k8s/00-build.yaml", "App.java"))
open("c/init/init.sql", "w").write(block("k8s/10-app.yaml", "init.sql"))
open("c/load/load.py", "w").write(block("k8s/20-load.yaml", "load.py"))
PY

echo "== What the setting changes, rendered from the chart"
CHART_VERSION=$(grep -m1 -oE -- '--version [0-9.]+' reproduce.sh | cut -d' ' -f2)
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null
helm repo update >/dev/null
render() {
  helm template lab splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector --version "$CHART_VERSION" --namespace splunk \
    --set splunkObservability.realm=us0 --set splunkObservability.accessToken=not-a-token --set clusterName=check \
    --set environment=check --set cloudProvider=aws --set distribution=eks -f k8s/collector-tap.yaml "$@"
}
render > c/off.yaml
render --set obi.enabled=true > c/on.yaml
render --set obi.enabled=true --set-string obi.env.OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION=headers > c/headers.yaml
[ "$(grep -c 'ebpf-instrument:' c/off.yaml || true)" -eq 0 ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: OBI renders while the setting is off"; exit 1; }
OBI_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'ghcr\.io/[^ "]*ebpf-instrument:[^ "]+' c/on.yaml || true)
[ -n "$OBI_IMAGE" ] || { echo "CHECK FAILED: obi.enabled=true rendered no OBI image"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION' c/headers.yaml || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the propagation value did not render"; exit 1; }
grep -q 'context_propagation\|OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION' c/on.yaml && echo "propagation set by the one setting: yes" || echo "propagation set by the one setting: no"
grep -q 'traces/tap:' c/on.yaml && grep -q 'otlp_http' c/on.yaml || { echo "CHECK FAILED: the tap or the Splunk export is missing from the agent config"; exit 1; }
COL_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'quay\.io/signalfx/splunk-otel-collector:[^ "]+' c/on.yaml || true)
echo "chart $CHART_VERSION, OBI image $OBI_IMAGE, Collector image $COL_IMAGE"
grep -E '^ +(hostPID|hostNetwork|privileged): ' c/on.yaml | sort -u
echo "objects the setting adds:"
diff <(grep -E '^kind: ' c/off.yaml | sort) <(grep -E '^kind: ' c/on.yaml | sort) | grep '^>' || true

IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'maven:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
PY_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ ]+' k8s/20-load.yaml)
PG_IMAGE=$(grep -m1 -oE 'postgres:[^ ]+' k8s/10-app.yaml)
docker network create lab >/dev/null

echo "== Building the jar"
docker run --rm -v "$PWD/c/src:/src:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab" "$IMAGE" sh -c '
  set -e; mkdir -p /w/src/main/java/lab; cp /src/pom.xml /w/; cp /src/App.java /w/src/main/java/lab/; cd /w
  mvn -q -B -DskipTests package; cp target/app.jar /lab/app.jar'
ls -l c/out

docker run -d --name postgres --network lab -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=lab -v "$PWD/c/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro" "$PG_IMAGE" >/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 30); do docker exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
sleep 3

start() {
  docker run -d --name "$1" --network lab -v "$PWD/c/out:/lab:ro" --entrypoint java -e "OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=$1" \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL=jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/postgres -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME=postgres \
    -e SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD=lab -e INVENTORY_URL=http://inventory:8080 \
    "$IMAGE" -Xms256m -Xmx256m -jar /lab/app.jar >/dev/null
}
ready() {
  for i in $(seq 1 60); do docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' && break; sleep 1; done
  docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | grep -q 'process running for' || { docker logs "$1" 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: $1 didn't start"; exit 1; }
}
load() { docker run --rm --name load --network lab -v "$PWD/c/load:/load:ro" -e SECONDS_TOTAL=15 -e SECONDS_WARM=2 "$PY_IMAGE" python /load/load.py; }
state() { docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} {{.Id}} {{.State.StartedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' orders inventory postgres; }
agents() { docker exec "$1" grep -c libinstrument /proc/1/maps || true; }

echo "== The services start with OBI off, and they keep running from here on"
start inventory
start orders
ready inventory
ready orders
load | tee c/off.txt
grep -q 'errors=0' c/off.txt || { docker logs orders 2>&1 | tail -30; echo "CHECK FAILED: requests failed with OBI off"; exit 1; }
state > c/state-before.txt
echo "Java agents loaded before OBI: orders $(agents orders), inventory $(agents inventory)"

cat > c/tap.yaml <<'YAML'
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 127.0.0.1:4318
exporters:
  debug/tap:
    verbosity: normal
    use_internal_logger: false
service:
  pipelines:
    traces/tap:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [debug/tap]
YAML
chmod 644 c/tap.yaml
KNOWN=4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736
known() { docker run --rm --network lab "$PY_IMAGE" python -c "import urllib.request as u; u.urlopen(u.Request('http://orders:8080/orders/1', headers={'traceparent': '00-$KNOWN-00f067aa0ba902b7-01'}), timeout=5).read()" || true; }

obi_run() {   # label, then any -e settings. OBI runs as the chart runs it, exporting to the same tap the lab reads on EKS
  local label=$1 i n
  shift
  docker run -d --name tap --network=host -v "$PWD/c/tap.yaml:/etc/tap.yaml:ro" "$COL_IMAGE" --config=/etc/tap.yaml >/dev/null || true
  sleep 3
  docker run -d --name obi --privileged --pid=host --network=host -v /sys/fs/cgroup:/sys/fs/cgroup:ro \
    -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318 -e OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf \
    -v /sys/kernel/tracing:/sys/kernel/tracing -v /sys/kernel/security:/sys/kernel/security:ro \
    -e OTEL_EBPF_TRACE_PRINTER=text -e OTEL_EBPF_OPEN_PORT=8080 -e OTEL_EBPF_LOG_LEVEL=info "$@" "$OBI_IMAGE" >/dev/null
  n=0
  for i in $(seq 1 45); do
    n=$(docker logs obi 2>&1 | grep -c 'instrumenting process' || true)
    [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && break
    sleep 2
  done
  echo "JVMs OBI reports instrumenting in the $label run: $n"
  sleep 15
  load | tee "c/$label.txt" || echo "the load stopped early in the $label run"
  known
  sleep 8
  docker logs obi > "c/$label.log" 2>&1
  docker rm -f obi >/dev/null
  sleep 2
  docker logs tap 2>/dev/null | tap_parse > "c/tap-$label.txt" || true
  docker logs tap 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -iE 'error|fatal' | cut -c1-190 | tail -3 || true
  docker rm -f tap >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  (cd c && tap_ids "tap-$label.txt" "$label" 2>&1) || true
  echo "$label: traced under the ID the caller sent: $(grep -c "$KNOWN" "c/tap-$label.txt" || true)"
  grep -E 'instrumenting process|java agent|java injection|capabilit|level=ERROR' "c/$label.log" | cut -c1-190 | tail -6 || true
  python3 - "$label" <<'PY'
import re, sys
label = sys.argv[1]
span = re.compile(r"\) (HTTP|HTTPClient|SQLClient)\(subType=\d+\) (\S*) (\S*) (\S*).*?traceparent=\[00-([0-9a-f]{32})-")
kinds = {"orders": set(), "inventory": set(), "client": 0, "sql": 0}
for line in open(f"c/{label}.log", errors="replace"):
    m = span.search(line)
    if not m:
        continue
    kind, _, _, path, trace = m.groups()
    if kind == "HTTP" and path.startswith("/orders/"):
        kinds["orders"].add(trace)
    elif kind == "HTTP" and path.startswith("/stock/"):
        kinds["inventory"].add(trace)
    elif kind == "HTTPClient" and path.startswith("/stock/"):
        kinds["client"] += 1
    elif kind == "SQLClient":
        kinds["sql"] += 1
joined = len(kinds["orders"] & kinds["inventory"])
print(f"{label}: orders traces {len(kinds['orders'])}, inventory traces {len(kinds['inventory'])}, client spans {kinds['client']}, SQL spans {kinds['sql']}, joined {joined}")
open(f"c/{label}.counts", "w").write(f"{len(kinds['orders'])} {len(kinds['inventory'])}\n")
PY
}

echo "== OBI starts against the running services, with the chart's own settings"
obi_run default
echo "Java agents loaded after OBI: orders $(agents orders), inventory $(agents inventory)"
read -r seen_orders seen_inventory < c/default.counts
[ "$seen_orders" -gt 0 ] && [ "$seen_inventory" -gt 0 ] || { tail -30 c/default.log | cut -c1-200; echo "CHECK FAILED: OBI saw no spans from a running service"; exit 1; }

echo "== Two more runs, with the same-host shortcut off, as for services on different nodes"
obi_run crossnode -e OTEL_EBPF_BPF_DISABLE_BLACK_BOX_CP=true
obi_run headers -e OTEL_EBPF_BPF_DISABLE_BLACK_BOX_CP=true -e OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION=headers
grep -H -o 'errors=[0-9]*' c/default.txt c/crossnode.txt c/headers.txt || true

echo "== The same containers, with no restart"
state > c/state-after.txt
cat c/state-after.txt
cmp c/state-before.txt c/state-after.txt || { echo "CHECK FAILED: a container restarted"; exit 1; }
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BUILD: one Helm value turns on OBI, and nothing in the demo namespace is touched. The map and restart results come from that value alone.
# Five OFF rounds end reproduce.sh, five ON rounds run here, and the Collector tap goes in after them.
# OBI assigns its own trace IDs, so each trace case reads them from its exported spans: one round, TRACE_WAIT, then 30 traces, misses twice.
# Each case waits the same, and the first case's wait overlaps propagate.sh, which adds the second value and runs its round.
# Time plan of 830s: before-check 15, first value 40, warm-up and ON rounds 205, tap 45, first round 45, propagate.sh 100 of its 170,
# then each read at TRACE_WAIT after its round, 50 each. It ends near 715. propagate.sh needs 380s left, or it reports -1.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=830
HERO_DONE=0
export TRACE_WAIT=200
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_fixed; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_fixed"; }' EXIT

source ./lib.sh
aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_API_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_API_TOKEN is not set"
export API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt) || fail "no load node recorded"
export LOAD_NODE
export CHART="splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector --version 0.163.1"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1

echo "== 2. The before-check: the cluster reaches Splunk, and the map is empty"
cluster=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 40 ]; do
  cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
echo "cluster metric time series in Splunk: ${cluster:-0}"
[ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] || fail "no cluster data reached Splunk, so an empty map would prove nothing"
before=$(on_map "$(topology)")
echo "services on the map before the change: ${before:-0}"
[ "${before:-0}" -eq 0 ] || fail "the map already held these services, so the comparison would be unfair"
ids=$(terraform output -raw node_instance_ids 2>/dev/null)
credits=$(aws ec2 describe-instance-credit-specifications --instance-ids $ids --query 'InstanceCreditSpecifications[].CpuCredits' --output text 2>/dev/null | tr '\t' ' ')
echo "instance CPU credit mode: ${credits:-not readable here}"

echo "== 4. The first value"
echo "helm upgrade --reuse-values --set obi.enabled=true"
helm upgrade splunk-otel-collector $CHART --namespace splunk --reuse-values --set obi.enabled=true >/dev/null || fail "helm upgrade failed"
obi_ready 70 30
helm list -n splunk -o json | jq -r '.[] | "\(.name) \(.chart) app \(.app_version)"'
kubectl -n splunk get ds -l app.kubernetes.io/name=obi -o json | jq -r '.items[0].spec.template.spec as $s | "OBI hostPID=\($s.hostPID) hostNetwork=\($s.hostNetwork) privileged=\($s.containers[0].securityContext.privileged)"'
obi_settings
obi_log | grep -E 'instrumenting process|java agent|java injection|capabilit|level=ERROR' | cut -c1-200 | tail -10

echo "== 5. One discarded round while OBI settles, then five rounds with OBI on, on the same pods"
echo "tap lines in the agent config during the timed rounds: $(tap_lines)"
: > load-settle.txt
load_round load-settle.txt
: > load-on.txt
for n in 1 2 3 4 5; do round load-on.txt ON; done
pods_now | tee pods-obi.txt
for s in orders inventory; do
  loaded=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$(newest "$s")" -c app -- grep -c libinstrument /proc/1/maps 2>/dev/null || true)
  echo "$loaded" > "helper-$s.txt"
  echo "$s Java agent mappings after OBI: ${loaded:-0}"
done

echo "== 6. The Collector tap and the first trace round"
helm upgrade splunk-otel-collector $CHART --namespace splunk --reuse-values -f k8s/collector-tap.yaml >/dev/null || fail "could not add the tap"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout=60s >/dev/null || fail "the Collector did not roll out"
echo "tap lines in the agent config for the trace rounds: $(tap_lines)"
echo "helm values under obi, unchanged: $(helm get values splunk-otel-collector -n splunk -o json | jq -c '.obi // {}')"
: > load-trace.txt
on_start=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
load_round load-trace.txt
on_end=$(date +%s)
tap_snapshot default "$on_start"
one_value_end=$(date +%s)   # the first value's map ends here

echo "== 7. The second value, in propagate.sh, while the first case waits"
if [ "$(remaining)" -ge 380 ]; then
  timeout 170 bash ./propagate.sh
else
  echo "propagate.sh did not start: only $(remaining)s left, and it needs 380s"
fi
wait_for() { local left=$(( $1 - $(date +%s) )); [ "$left" -gt 0 ] && sleep "$left"; }

echo "== 7b. Reading each case ${TRACE_WAIT}s after its round"
wait_for $(( on_end + TRACE_WAIT ))
read -r default_found default_joined default_searched < <(bash ./propagate.sh read default)
if [ -s propagate-result.txt ]; then
  read -r prop_start prop_end < propagate-result.txt
  wait_for $(( prop_end + TRACE_WAIT ))
  read -r prop_found prop_joined prop_searched < <(bash ./propagate.sh read propagation)
else
  prop_found=0; prop_joined=0; prop_searched=0
fi
pods_now > pods-final.txt
later() { if [ -s propagate-result.txt ]; then restarts_by_pod pods-obi.txt pods-final.txt; else printf '%s -1\n' inventory orders postgres; fi; }

echo "== 8. The result"
map=$(topology "$one_value_end")   # this window ends before the second value
services=$(on_map "$map"); own=$(on_map "$map" own)
show_map "$map"
echo "map nodes and inferred flag, first value window: $(map_nodes "$map")"
[ -s propagate-result.txt ] && echo "map nodes and inferred flag, second value window only: $(map_nodes "$(topology "$(date +%s)" "$prop_start")")"
echo "services with their own request metric: $(series "sf_metric:service.request.count AND sf_environment:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -c '[.results[]?.dimensions.sf_service // empty] | unique' 2>/dev/null)"
kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,KERNEL:.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion,OS:.status.nodeInfo.osImage'
pods_now
[ "$(grep -c . pods-obi.txt)" -eq 3 ] && [ "$(grep -c . pods-final.txt)" -eq 3 ] || fail "a pod is gone"
echo "services with own spans on the first value map, the headline figure: ${own:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: services_with_own_spans=${own:-0}"
echo "services on map from Splunk, inferred nodes included: ${services:-0}"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: services_on_map=${services:-0}"
restarts=0
while read -r pod n; do
  echo "$pod pod restarts added by the first value: $n"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: pod_restarts_added[$pod]=$n"
  restarts=$(( restarts + n ))
done < <(restarts_by_pod pods-before.txt pods-obi.txt)
while read -r pod n; do
  echo "$pod pod restarts after propagation, -1 means not run: $n"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: pod_restarts_after_propagation[$pod]=$n"
done < <(later)
echo "traces joined default ${default_joined} found ${default_found} of ${default_searched}, joined propagation ${prop_joined} found ${prop_found} of ${prop_searched}"
for m in joined_default:$default_joined found_default:$default_found joined_propagation:$prop_joined found_propagation:$prop_found; do echo "HERO_MEASURE: traces_${m%%:*}=${m##*:}"; done
for s in orders inventory; do
  held=$(cat "helper-$s.txt")
  flag=$(( ${held:-0} > 0 ))
  echo "$s jvm helper attached: $flag"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: jvm_helper_attached[$s]=$flag"
done
off=$(p95s load-off.txt | sort -n)
on=$(p95s load-on.txt | sort -n)
echo "p95 with OBI off: min $(head -1 <<<"$off"), median $(sed -n 3p <<<"$off"), max $(tail -1 <<<"$off") ms"
echo "p95 with OBI on: min $(head -1 <<<"$on"), median $(sed -n 3p <<<"$on"), max $(tail -1 <<<"$on") ms"
added=$(awk -v a="$(sed -n 3p <<<"$on")" -v b="$(sed -n 3p <<<"$off")" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", a-b}')
echo "p95 added ms, medians of five rounds, about 20 requests a second: $added"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: p95_added_ms=$added"
noise=$(awk -v a="$(head -1 <<<"$off")" -v b="$(tail -1 <<<"$off")" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", b-a}')
echo "p95 noise ms, the spread of the five OFF rounds: $noise"
echo "HERO_MEASURE: p95_noise_ms=$noise"

if [ "${own:-0}" -ge 2 ] && [ "$restarts" -eq 0 ]; then
  emit fixed
else
  emit not_fixed
fi

    package lab;

    import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
    import org.springframework.boot.SpringApplication;
    import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.SpringBootApplication;
    import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate;

    import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.PathVariable;
    import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;
    import org.springframework.web.client.RestClient;

    @SpringBootApplication
    @RestController
    public class App {
      private final JdbcTemplate jdbc;
      private final RestClient inventory;

      public App(JdbcTemplate jdbc, RestClient.Builder builder, @Value("${inventory.url}") String url) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
        this.inventory = builder.baseUrl(url).build();

      }

# Puts the OBI image on a node before the measured stages, so a slow pull can't use up their time. It has no privileges and
# no host access, so OBI can't start here. Only the pull matters, and reproduce.sh deletes the pod after it.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: POD_NAME
  namespace: splunk
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: NODE_NAME

# A measuring aid. fix.sh adds it to the agent after the timed rounds, so no latency figure includes it. OBI's settings and the
# export to Splunk don't change. OBI assigns its own trace IDs, so only its exported spans can say which traces to read back.
# This second pipeline writes one line per span to the agent's log. Leave it out of your own cluster.
agent:
  config:
    exporters:
      debug/tap:
        verbosity: normal
        use_internal_logger: false   # the internal logger samples its output, and this needs every line
    service:
      pipelines:
        traces/tap:
          receivers: [otlp]
          exporters: [debug/tap]

kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
data:
  load.py: |
    # Sends one order request every 50 ms. Each carries a traceparent, as an instrumented caller would, and the lab never relies on those IDs.
    import http.client, os, random, sys, time
    seconds, warm = int(os.environ["SECONDS_TOTAL"]), int(os.environ["SECONDS_WARM"])
    conn, took, errors, gap = http.client.HTTPConnection("orders", 8080, timeout=10), [], 0, 0.05
    def cpu():
        with open("/proc/stat") as f:
            v = [int(x) for x in f.readline().split()[1:]]
        return sum(v), v[3] + v[4]
    cpu_start, start = cpu(), time.time()
    while time.time() - start < seconds:
        sent = time.time()
        last = "%032x" % random.getrandbits(128)
        try:
            conn.request("GET", "/orders/%d" % random.randint(1, 1000), headers={"traceparent": "00-%s-%016x-01" % (last, random.getrandbits(64))})
            r = conn.getresponse(); r.read()
            ok = r.status == 200
        except Exception:
            ok = False
            conn.close()
        ms = (time.time() - sent) * 1000
        if not ok:
            errors += 1
        elif sent - start >= warm:
            took.append(ms)
        time.sleep(max(0, gap - ms / 1000))
    cpu_end = cpu()
    print("LOAD node_busy_pct=%.0f" % (100 * (1 - (cpu_end[1] - cpu_start[1]) / max(1, cpu_end[0] - cpu_start[0]))))
    took.sort()
    if not took:
        print("LOAD no successful requests after warm-up, errors=%d" % errors)
        sys.exit(1)
    print("LOAD requests=%d errors=%d p50_ms=%.2f p95_ms=%.2f" % (len(took), errors, took[len(took) // 2], took[int(len(took) * 0.95)]))
---

metadata:

  namespace: demo
spec:

  volumes:
    - name: load

        name: load
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["python", "/load/load.py"]
      env:
        - { name: SECONDS_TOTAL, value: "20" }
        - { name: SECONDS_WARM, value: "5" }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The second value, in its own script with its own time limit. fix.sh starts it under `timeout`, while the first case waits.
# It sets the value, runs one load round and saves what OBI exported. fix.sh then reads the traces TRACE_WAIT after the round.
# It writes propagate-result.txt only when every step finished, so anything else is reported as -1, not run.
# `propagate.sh read <label>` is the other job here: it reads one case's traces, the same way for both.
# LIMIT 170s: helm and rollout 65, load round 35, snapshot 10, which leaves about 60 spare.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=170
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL in propagate.sh: $*"; exit 0; }

source ./lib.sh

api_get() {   # path, file. Saves the body and prints "status seconds", or 000 for a timeout
  curl -sS --max-time 8 -o "$2" -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}' -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API$1" 2>/dev/null || true
}

one_trace() {   # trace ID, folder, pass. Saves a trace holding orders or inventory, or logs why not
  local f="$2/$1" raw n a b="" seg
  a=$(api_get "/v2/apm/trace/$1/latest" "$f.latest")
  raw=$(cat "$f.latest" 2>/dev/null)
  if ! jq -e 'type == "array" and length > 0' <<<"$raw" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    b=$(api_get "/v2/apm/trace/$1/segments" "$f.seg")
    raw=$(for seg in $(jq -r '.[]?' "$f.seg" 2>/dev/null); do curl -sS --max-time 8 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/$seg" 2>/dev/null; done | jq -s 'map(if type == "array" then . else [] end) | add // []' 2>/dev/null)
  fi
  echo "${a#* } ${b#* }" >> "$2/times"
  n=$(jq -r --arg a "$APPS" '[(if type == "array" then . else (.spans // []) end)[] | (.serviceName // .service // .localEndpoint.serviceName // empty) | select(test($a))] | unique | length' <<<"$raw" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "${n:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then echo "$raw" > "$f.json"; echo "$n" > "$f.count"
  else echo "pass $3 latest ${a%% *}, $(wc -c < "$f.latest" 2>/dev/null) bytes, segments ${b%% *}" >> "$2/misses"; fi
}

read_ids() {   # folder, pass, ID file. Eight at a time, stopping after 40 seconds
  local id i=0 from
  from=$(date +%s)
  for id in $(cat "$3"); do
    [ $(( $(date +%s) - from )) -lt 40 ] || break
    [ -e "$1/$id.count" ] && continue
    one_trace "$id" "$1" "$2" &
    i=$(( i + 1 ))
    [ $(( i % 8 )) -eq 0 ] && wait
  done
  wait
  echo "$1 pass $2, oldest first, F found: $(while read -r id; do [ -e "$1/$id.count" ] && printf F || printf .; done < "$3")" >&2
}

trace_pass() {   # label. 30 evenly spaced orders traces, then each miss once more 15s later, the same in both cases.
  # Prints "traces found, traces joined, IDs searched", the misses, and one sample trace.
  local dir="traces-$1" found joined sample n step
  rm -rf "$dir"; mkdir -p "$dir"
  n=$(grep -c . "ids-$1.txt")
  step=$(( n > 30 ? n / 30 : 1 ))
  awk -v s="$step" 'NR % s == 0' "ids-$1.txt" | head -30 > "sample-$1.txt"
  read_ids "$dir" 1 "sample-$1.txt"
  sleep 15
  read_ids "$dir" 2 "sample-$1.txt"
  { sort "$dir/misses" 2>/dev/null | uniq -c | sed "s/^/$1 misses: /"
    echo "$1 lookup seconds, slowest: $(tr ' ' '\n' < "$dir/times" 2>/dev/null | grep . | sort -n | tail -1), at the 8s limit: $(grep -c '8\.[0-9]' "$dir/times" 2>/dev/null)"; } >&2
  found=$(ls "$dir" | grep -c '\.count$' || true)
  joined=$(cat "$dir"/*.count 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^2$' || true)
  sample=$(grep -l '^2$' "$dir"/*.count 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  [ -n "$sample" ] || sample=$(ls "$dir"/*.count 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  if [ -n "$sample" ]; then
    echo "sample trace from the $1 case: $(basename "$sample" .count)" >&2
    jq -r 'if type == "array" then .[] else .spans[]? end | "  \(.serviceName) \(.operationName) span=\(.spanId // "?") parent=\(.parentId // "none")"' "${sample%.count}.json" 2>/dev/null | head -12 >&2
    jq -c 'if type == "array" then .[0] else .spans[0] end' "${sample%.count}.json" 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-420 >&2
  else
    echo "sample trace from the $1 case: none found" >&2
  fi
  echo "${found:-0} ${joined:-0} $(grep -c . "sample-$1.txt")"
}

if [ "${1:-}" = read ]; then
  trace_pass "$2"
  exit 0
fi

rm -f propagate-result.txt

echo "helm upgrade --reuse-values --set-string obi.env.OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION=headers"
helm upgrade splunk-otel-collector $CHART --namespace splunk --reuse-values --set-string obi.env.OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION=headers >/dev/null || fail "helm upgrade failed"
obi_ready 60 20
obi_settings
obi_log | grep -iE 'propagation' | cut -c1-200 | tail -4
kubectl -n splunk get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=obi -o json | jq -e '[.items[].spec.containers[0].env[] | select(.name == "OTEL_EBPF_BPF_CONTEXT_PROPAGATION" and .value == "headers")] | length >= 2' >/dev/null || fail "the running OBI pods do not hold the propagation value"

: > load-prop.txt
prop_start=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
first=$(date +%s)
load_round load-prop.txt
ended=$(date +%s)
tap_snapshot propagation "$prop_start"
echo "$first $ended" > propagate-result.txt

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE: orders calls inventory across two nodes, and inventory reads Postgres. The Collector runs, and OBI is off.
# These pods stay up. fix.sh has to put them on the Splunk APM map without touching them.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

START=$(date +%s)
LIMIT=810
HERO_DONE=0
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit not_reproduced; exit 0; }
trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: not_reproduced"; }' EXIT

source ./lib.sh
aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"

# EKS gets a third node for the load. The free rehearsal has two, so the load shares a node there.
want=$(terraform output -raw node_count 2>/dev/null)
[[ "$want" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || want=2
echo "== 1. Waiting for $want worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge "$want" ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,ARCH:.status.nodeInfo.architecture,KERNEL:.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion,OS:.status.nodeInfo.osImage,RUNTIME:.status.nodeInfo.containerRuntimeVersion' || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge "$want" ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 500)s" || true

# orders and inventory run on different nodes, so a trace can only join by crossing the network, as it would in a real cluster.
ORDERS_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
INVENTORY_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[2].metadata.name}')
[ -n "$LOAD_NODE" ] || LOAD_NODE=$INVENTORY_NODE
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "orders node: $ORDERS_NODE"
echo "inventory and postgres node: $INVENTORY_NODE"
echo "load node: $LOAD_NODE"

[ -n "${SPLUNK_REALM:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_REALM is not set"
[ -n "${SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ] || fail "SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN is not set"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1) with OBI at its default, off"
helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1
helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set environment="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 500)s" || fail "collector agent not ready"
echo "OBI pods running: $(kubectl -n splunk get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=obi --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c . || true)"

echo "== 2b. Pulling the OBI image onto every node, so its pull can't eat into the measured stages"
OBI_IMAGE=$(helm template lab splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector --version 0.163.1 --set splunkObservability.realm=us0 --set splunkObservability.accessToken=not-a-token --set clusterName=pull --set obi.enabled=true 2>/dev/null | grep -m1 -oE 'ghcr\.io/[^ "]*ebpf-instrument:[^ "]+')
if [ -n "$OBI_IMAGE" ]; then
  n=0
  for node in $(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
    n=$(( n + 1 ))
    sed -e "s/POD_NAME/pull-$n/" -e "s/NODE_NAME/$node/" -e "s|OBI_IMAGE|$OBI_IMAGE|" k8s/05-prepull.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the image pull"
  done
  have=0
  for i in $(seq 1 48); do
    have=$(kubectl -n splunk get pods -o json | jq '[.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^pull-")) | select(.status.containerStatuses[0].imageID // "" | length > 0)] | length')
    [ "${have:-0}" -ge "$n" ] && break
    sleep 5
  done
  echo "OBI image $OBI_IMAGE on $have of $n nodes"
  kubectl -n splunk get pods -o name | grep '/pull-' | xargs -r kubectl -n splunk delete --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
else
  echo "could not read the OBI image from the chart, so OBI will pull it when it starts"
fi

echo "== 3. Building the jar once on each node"
for n in a b; do
  node=$ORDERS_NODE
  [ "$n" = b ] && node=$INVENTORY_NODE
  sed -e "s/BUILD_NAME/build-$n/" -e "s/BUILD_NODE/$node/" k8s/00-build.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the build"
done
done_jobs=0
t0=$(date +%s)
limit=$(cap 430 330)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$limit" ]; do
  kubectl -n demo get jobs -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null | grep -q Failed && break
  done_jobs=$(kubectl -n demo get jobs -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.status=="True")].type}' 2>/dev/null | grep -o Complete | grep -c . || true)
  [ "${done_jobs:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl -n demo logs job/build-a --tail=5 2>/dev/null || true
[ "${done_jobs:-0}" -ge 2 ] || { kubectl -n demo describe jobs | tail -15; fail "the builds did not finish"; }
echo "both builds took $(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))s"

echo "== 4. Deploying Postgres, orders and inventory"
sed -e "s/ORDERS_NODE/$ORDERS_NODE/" -e "s/INVENTORY_NODE/$INVENTORY_NODE/" k8s/10-app.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the app"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/postgres --timeout="$(cap 90 240)s" || fail "postgres did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/inventory --timeout="$(cap 120 220)s" || fail "inventory did not start"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/orders --timeout="$(cap 120 210)s" || fail "orders did not start"

echo "== 5. The JVMs before OBI"
for s in orders inventory; do
  p=$(newest "$s")
  echo "$s image: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}')"
  echo "$s JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS or OTEL settings: $(kubectl -n demo get "$p" -o json | jq '[.spec.containers[0].env[].name | select(test("^(JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS|OTEL_)"))] | length')"
  loaded=$(kubectl -n demo exec "$p" -c app -- grep -c libinstrument /proc/1/maps 2>/dev/null || true)
  echo "$s Java agents loaded: ${loaded:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: jvm_helper_before[$s]=$(( ${loaded:-0} > 0 ))"
done

echo "== 6. Warming the JVMs, then five rounds with OBI off, ending seconds before the change in fix.sh"
: > load-warmup.txt
for round in 1 2; do load_round load-warmup.txt; done
grep -q 'errors=0' load-warmup.txt || fail "requests failed before any change"
: > load-off.txt
for n in 1 2 3 4 5; do round load-off.txt OFF; done

echo "== 7. The pods as they stand: name, UID, restarts, container start time, image"
pods_now | tee pods-before.txt
[ "$(grep -c . pods-before.txt)" -eq 3 ] || fail "expected 3 pods"

emit reproduced
